question: Why is the home health nurse often described as the central communication hub?

options.A: They make all final medical diagnoses without consulting a physician
options.B: They are the only healthcare worker allowed to visit the residence
options.C: They manage the central telephone switchboard for the health agency
options.D: They connect the patient, family, doctors, and therapists together

explanation: Because nurses visit frequently, they coordinate information between all the different disciplines involved in the patient's care. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h6)

question: How can taking unregulated herbal remedies during pregnancy lead to birth defects?

options.A: They cause an immediate miscarriage without touching fetal structure
options.B: They may contain teratogens that disrupt baby's organ formation
options.C: They speed up the growth of the placenta too quickly
options.D: They permanently lower the mother's blood pressure

explanation: Substances that mess with normal development are called teratogens. Many local herbal mixes haven't been safety-tested for pregnancy, so it's always safer to stick to prescribed antenatal vitamins!

question: Why must nurses look at the whole person—not just physical symptoms—when caring for palliative patients?

options.A: Physical pain never occurs without accompanying fever.
options.B: Physical symptoms are often worsened by emotional and spiritual distress.
options.C: Medications only work if the patient is sleeping soundly.
options.D: Lab tests can detect all forms of human suffering.

explanation: Everything is connected! When a patient is worried, scared, or spiritually troubled, their physical pain often feels much worse. Holistic care means healing the whole person.

question: What does true community integration mean for a person living with a physical disability?

options.A: Actively participating in local social, religious, and economic life
options.B: Staying inside a specialized care facility with other patients
options.C: Relying solely on family members for all social interactions
options.D: Traveling abroad to access better rehabilitation centers

explanation: Spot on! True inclusion is more than just living somewhere—it's being actively involved in community activities and relationships.

question: Why should hospital waste bags be tied up when they are only three-quarters full?

options.A: To ensure the waste weighs exactly the same as household garbage
options.B: To prevent overfilling, tearing, and accidental spills during transit
options.C: To give the cleaning staff enough time to take a lunch break
options.D: To allow the municipal collection agency to charge lower fees

explanation: Exactly! Leaving a bit of space at the top lets you tie the bag securely and stops nasty spills on the way out.

question: Which health problem is most commonly linked to severe FGM over a woman's lifetime?

options.A: Rapid onset of Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Complete loss of vision within ten years
options.C: High blood pressure and sudden heart failure
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain and childbirth complications

explanation: Great job! The physical trauma and scarring from FGM frequently cause long-term pain, difficult menstruation, and severe troubles during childbirth. You're doing great!

question: Which of these is NOT one of the four main tissue types in the human body?

options.A: Epithelial tissue
options.B: Nervous tissue
options.C: Adipose tissue
options.D: Connective tissue

explanation: Adipose (fat) tissue is actually a type of connective tissue, not one of the four big primary tissue categories.

question: What is the very first step of urine formation in the kidney?

options.A: Tubular secretion
options.B: Glomerular filtration
options.C: Peristaltic propulsion
options.D: Tubular reabsorption

explanation: Everything starts at the glomerulus! Blood pressure forces water and small particles out of the blood and into Bowman's capsule to kick off urine making.

question: What is the primary goal of patient safety measures in a hospital?

options.A: To prevent harm and medical errors during care
options.B: To lower the cost of purchasing medical drugs
options.C: To speed up the discharge process for doctors
options.D: To reduce the total number of hospital beds

explanation: Patient safety is centered entirely on stopping avoidable injuries and medical mistakes before they harm the person receiving treatment. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T7#GNS112_U4_T7_h1)

question: What common foot problem does a footboard primarily prevent in patients who are on bed rest?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Pressure ulcers on the heels
options.C: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.D: Foot drop

explanation: Brilliant! A footboard holds the feet in a natural upright position, stopping the Achilles tendon from tightening up and causing permanent foot drop.

question: What is the main job of our skin, hair, and nails (the integumentary system)?

options.A: Regulating red blood cell production in bone marrow
options.B: Facilitating conscious voluntary muscle movement
options.C: Synthesizing essential water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Protecting the body from environmental hazards

explanation: Think of your skin as your body's personal security guard! It is your first line of defense against germs, harsh chemicals, and physical injury.

question: What is the job of the air inlet on a Nelson inhaler?

options.A: It locks the cork lid tightly into the ceramic jar
options.B: It lets the nurse pour medicine in while treating
options.C: It acts as a drain for extra water collection
options.D: It allows fresh air to mix with the rising steam

explanation: Exactly! The air inlet lets a bit of cooler room air mix with the vapor. This keeps the steam from being too scorching hot for the patient's mouth and throat.

question: A pregnant client shares that she drank a local root mix to prevent pregnancy before realizing she was already conceiving. How should you respond?

options.A: Report the local healer immediately to local law enforcement authorities
options.B: Assess for any adverse side effects and provide supportive prenatal guidance
options.C: Scold the client harshly for ignoring modern hospital medications
options.D: Assume the pregnancy is completely unaffected without asking questions

explanation: Always keep a warm, non-judgmental attitude. Check in on her symptoms to ensure she's safe, and give her loving prenatal support.

question: What process does a sublingual drug successfully avoid by entering the bloodstream directly?

options.A: Gastric acid destruction
options.B: First-pass metabolism
options.C: Renal excretion
options.D: Pulmonary filtration

explanation: Great job! Because it skips the liver's initial breakdown (first-pass metabolism), more active drug reaches your patient.

question: Why do modern nurses prefer keeping a wound environment moist?

options.A: It leaves the wound completely open to fresh air safely.
options.B: It keeps the body from producing any fluid at all.
options.C: It stops all bacterial growth on the skin completely.
options.D: It lets skin cells repair faster and helps prevent harsh scarring.

explanation: Skin cells love moisture! They glide across a moist wound bed way faster than trying to crawl across a dry, crusty scab. Great nursing knowledge to keep in your pocket.

question: What is the most frequent cause of nephrotic syndrome in young children?

options.A: Membranous nephropathy
options.B: Systemic lupus erythematosus
options.C: Minimal change disease
options.D: Focal segmental glomerulosclerosis

explanation: Minimal change disease accounts for the vast majority of nephrotic syndrome cases in children and usually responds very well to steroid therapy. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h2)

question: Why is noting a patient's biological sex important when taking an endocrine history?

options.A: It helps identify conditions like thyroid disorders that affect women more often
options.B: It dictates the exact calorie count the patient needs daily
options.C: It replaces the need to perform a complete review of systems
options.D: It proves whether the patient has a genetic metabolic disease

explanation: Well done! Knowing biological sex helps us suspect certain gender-linked conditions, like thyroid imbalances, right from the start.

question: Why shouldn't you crush enteric-coated oral tablets?

options.A: Crushing destroys the protective coating, which can irritate the stomach or ruin the drug's timed release
options.B: It changes the pill color, which confuses the pharmacy department
options.C: It makes the pill powder too sweet for the patient to swallow comfortably
options.D: The crushed powder will instantly clog standard drinking straws

explanation: That special coating is there for a reason! It protects the stomach lining and controls how fast the drug dissolves. Crushing ruins that design.

question: What is the main danger of atrial fibrillation?

options.A: The lungs fill with thick mucus
options.B: The heart stops all electrical activity forever
options.C: Blood can pool in the heart and form dangerous clots
options.D: Blood pressure rises past 200

explanation: In A-fib, the upper chambers of the heart just quiver instead of squeezing properly. When blood sits still like that, it forms clots that can travel to the brain. Scary stuff, but totally makes sense when you picture it!

question: What is the primary psychiatric condition that antipsychotic medications were originally developed to treat?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Schizophrenia
options.C: Essential hypertension
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Schizophrenia is the main condition these drugs were designed for. They help patients manage reality-distorting symptoms so they can function better.

question: What hormone directly stimulates the initial growth and maturation of ovarian follicles?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Follicle-stimulating hormone

explanation: Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) is released by the pituitary gland to stimulate ovarian follicles to grow. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h5)

question: A nurse notices a stroke patient suddenly loses the ability to speak clearly and starts mixing up words. Which assessment priority is most urgent?

options.A: Inspecting the patient's skin for pressure ulcers
options.B: Checking the patient's hearing with a tuning fork
options.C: Evaluating language and speech areas in the brain
options.D: Testing lower leg reflexes with a percussion hammer

explanation: Sudden speech changes point to acute involvement of language centers like Broca's or Wernicke's areas, demanding prompt neurological tracking. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T23#GNS211_U3_T23_h7)

question: What important instruction should a nurse give a patient who has received dilating eye drops?

options.A: Wear heavy winter gloves to avoid rubbing the eyelids
options.B: Avoid driving because their vision will be temporarily blurred
options.C: Keep their eyes tightly closed for the rest of the day
options.D: Wash their eyes thoroughly with tap water every ten minutes

explanation: Dilating drops paralyze the focusing muscles and dilate the pupil, causing blurry vision and glare, making driving unsafe. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h5)

question: Which special test is commonly used by clinicians to assess for carpal tunnel syndrome at the wrist?

options.A: Phalen's test
options.B: Straight leg raise
options.C: Tendon reflex hammer test
options.D: McMurray's test

explanation: Phalen's test involves holding the wrists in acute flexion for 60 seconds to reproduce numbness and tingling associated with carpal tunnel syndrome. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h8)

question: A patient complains of sudden vulval redness and intense itching after starting a new brand of scented bubble bath. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A hormone-secreting ovarian tumor
options.B: A chronic autoimmune joint disorder
options.C: An irritant or allergic contact reaction
options.D: A congenital anatomical defect

explanation: Chemicals and fragrances in bubble baths often trigger contact dermatitis on the sensitive skin of the vulva. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h2)

question: How can long-term social isolation negatively affect an older adult?

options.A: It stops them from developing age-related illnesses
options.B: It permanently improves their ability to stay calm
options.C: It weakens immune function and worsens mental health
options.D: It increases their daily physical endurance levels

explanation: Humans are social creatures! Lack of connection causes chronic stress, which hurts both mental well-being and the immune system. Checking in on elderly patients matters.

question: Which medication is commonly administered intrathecally to treat central nervous system involvement in certain cancers?

options.A: Methotrexate
options.B: Morphine
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Heparin

explanation: Methotrexate is a frequent intrathecal chemotherapy agent used to reach cancer cells hiding behind the blood-brain barrier. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T10#GNS125_U3_T10_h3)

question: Which of these is part of the body's first line of defence?

options.A: Circulating blood antibodies
options.B: Intact skin and mucous membranes
options.C: Phagocytic white blood cells
options.D: Specialized T-lymphocyte cells

explanation: You got it! Your skin and mucous membranes act like a brick wall at the gate, stopping germs from entering your body in the first place.

question: Why are tiny finger-like projections called chorionic villi so important for a developing baby?

options.A: They prevent the mother's immune system from rejecting the fetus.
options.B: They greatly increase surface area for nutrient and gas exchange.
options.C: They produce all the amniotic fluid found in the amniotic sac.
options.D: They form the muscular walls of the uterus to prepare for labor.

explanation: Think of chorionic villi like the branching roots of a tree; their massive surface area makes it easy for the baby to absorb oxygen and food from the mother.

question: When holding vegetables to slice them, how should you position your non-dominant hand?

options.A: With fingertips curled inward in a claw grip
options.B: Holding the food loosely with only the thumb and index finger
options.C: With fingers pointed straight out toward the blade
options.D: Pressing the palm flat directly on top of the food item

explanation: The 'claw grip' tucks your fingertips safely behind your knuckles so the knife glides past them safely. Perfect technique!

question: What is a common emotional response a patient might experience after an abortion?

options.A: An immediate desire to write a public memoir about the event
options.B: Complete emotional numbness that lasts for an entire lifetime
options.C: A wide range of feelings including relief, grief, or anxiety
options.D: Permanent clinical detachment from all family members

explanation: Exactly! Feelings after pregnancy loss are deeply personal and can span anywhere from sadness and anxiety to relief.

question: What is the name of the thick, yellowish fluid the breasts produce in the later stages of pregnancy?

options.A: Foremilk
options.B: Lymph fluid
options.C: Colostrum
options.D: Mature milk

explanation: Colostrum is often called 'liquid gold'! It's packed with antibodies and nutrients, ready and waiting for the newborn.

question: Which part of the nervous system is responsible for triggering a penile erection?

options.A: Somatic motor nervous system
options.B: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Central spinal nervous system

explanation: Well done! The parasympathetic nervous system handles the 'rest and digest' actions, including sending signals that relax blood vessels so erectile tissue can fill with blood.

question: What is the primary cause of constipation and heartburn during pregnancy?

options.A: Complete cessation of digestive enzyme production in the stomach
options.B: Rapid over-activity of the bowel wall muscles
options.C: Relaxation of smooth muscle caused by elevated progesterone
options.D: Direct compression of the liver by the growing fetus

explanation: Progesterone slows down peristalsis throughout the gastrointestinal tract and relaxes the sphincter separating the stomach from the esophagus. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

question: What is the main sign that sets a food-borne intoxication apart from an infection?

options.A: Living parasites in the blood
options.B: Rapid onset of symptoms within hours
options.C: A long incubation period lasting weeks
options.D: High persistent fever as the very first sign

explanation: Because intoxications are caused by toxins already sitting in the food, your body reacts super fast—often within hours! You're crushing this.

question: Why does a ventilation-perfusion mismatch happen when someone has a severe lung infection?

options.A: Blocked air sacs still get blood flow, but can't get fresh air.
options.B: The throat swells up and stops breathing completely.
options.C: The heart pumps blood way too slowly for the lungs.
options.D: Mucus plugs in the windpipe block blood from reaching the heart.

explanation: Think of it as a mismatch: blood is flowing past the air sacs ready to pick up oxygen, but because they are full of fluid, there's no fresh air waiting for them.

question: Which of these findings is completely normal and NOT a sign of heart stress?

options.A: A resting heart rate of 120 beats per minute
options.B: A regular resting pulse rate of 75 beats per minute
options.C: A blood pressure reading consistently above 140/90 mmHg
options.D: An apex beat displaced far to the left of the midclavicular line

explanation: A pulse of 75 bpm sits right in the middle of the normal 60–100 range. Nothing to worry about here! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: What is the main job of the nephrons in the kidneys?

options.A: Transporting urine directly to the urethra
options.B: Storing urine until it leaves the body
options.C: Pumping blood through the lower back
options.D: Filtering the blood to form urine

explanation: You've got this! Nephrons are the tiny working units inside your kidneys that clean your blood and make urine.

question: What happens to the ovaries when the brain's hormonal axis (the HPO axis) gets disrupted?

options.A: Immediate cessation of blood flow to the uterus
options.B: Premature depletion of all body fat
options.C: Failure to ovulate regularly
options.D: Permanent enlargement of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Spot on! If the communication lines between the brain and ovaries get scrambled, the ovaries don't get the proper signals to release an egg every month.

question: A mother wants to stop her child's 5-day antibiotic course after 2 days because the fever stopped. What is your best response?

options.A: Explain that the full course must be finished to kill all bacteria and prevent resistance
options.B: Tell her to double the dose for the remaining days to make up for it
options.C: Agree that she can stop the medication since the fever is gone
options.D: Switch the child to an injectable antibiotic immediately

explanation: Always encourage patients to finish the full dose! Stopping early lets tough bacteria survive and bounce back stronger as drug-resistant strains.

question: Which workplace factor makes it hardest for employees to bring home-cooked food to their shift?

options.A: Lack of basic amenities like refrigerators and microwaves
options.B: The high cost of buying lunchboxes and food containers
options.C: Mandatory breaks that last less than two minutes
options.D: Company rules that forbid eating food brought from home

explanation: Without a safe place to store and heat food at work, employees have no choice but to buy outside meals or snack on dry foods. You're learning fast!

question: Why is tracing sexual partners and notifying them so important after an STI diagnosis?

options.A: It punishes individuals who fail to use proper barrier protection
options.B: It proves whether the patient acquired the infection locally
options.C: It breaks the cycle of reinfection and treats exposed individuals
options.D: It provides statistical data for insurance companies to adjust rates

explanation: Exactly! Partner notification ensures everyone gets tested and treated so they don't keep passing the infection back and forth.

question: Why is having family support especially helpful for patients managing HIV?

options.A: It lowers depression and improves treatment retention
options.B: It eliminates the need for routine laboratory testing
options.C: It removes any financial burden from the household
options.D: It completely cures the viral infection over time

explanation: Spot on! When loved ones offer emotional and everyday backing, it helps patients stay positive and stick to their medication schedules.

question: What primary part of the kidney is inflamed in Acute Glomerulonephritis?

options.A: The glomeruli
options.B: The renal pelvis
options.C: The loop of Henle
options.D: The ureteral walls

explanation: Acute Glomerulonephritis specifically targets and inflames the glomeruli, which are the primary filtering units of the kidneys. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T4#GNS213_U4_T4_h1)

question: What is a major duty of the health orderly in the operating theatre?

options.A: Counting surgical needles before wound closure
options.B: Scrubbing in to assist the surgeon at the table
options.C: Administering intravenous fluids and medications
options.D: Transporting patients and heavy supplies safely

explanation: Health orderlies are essential for smooth operations—they handle patient transport, heavy lifting, waste disposal, and moving equipment.

question: Which of these methods is NOT reliable for destroying infectious prions?

options.A: Using disposable instruments
options.B: Extended chemical disinfection
options.C: Standard boiling in water
options.D: Specialized high-heat autoclaving

explanation: Spot on! Prions are super tough and survive normal boiling. They need heavy-duty, specialized sterilization protocols to be destroyed.

question: Which landmark document formally launched the modern health promotion movement in 1986?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Abuja Declaration
options.C: The Nightingale Pledge
options.D: The Ottawa Charter

explanation: The Ottawa Charter of 1986 defined the core strategies for health promotion on a global scale. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why must a nurse remember that not every large or palpable mass in the genitourinary area is cancer?

options.A: Non-cancerous conditions like BPH can also create large, feelable masses
options.B: Malignant tumors are impossible to feel during a physical exam
options.C: Palpable masses are only ever caused by trapped fluid pockets
options.D: Benign growths always shrink on their own without any treatment

explanation: Conditions like benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) can make an organ swell up big enough to feel during an exam, which is why doctors always order tests like biopsies to be sure.

question: Which of the following is NOT a systemic risk associated with unsafe or unnecessary injections?

options.A: Systemic complications from contaminated equipment
options.B: Transmission of Hepatitis B and C viruses
options.C: Development of complete tolerance to oral painkillers
options.D: Acquisition of secondary bloodstream infections

explanation: Unsafe injections cause infections and bloodborne virus transmission, not oral drug tolerance. The question asks for what is NOT a risk. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T6#GNS122_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which nutritional deficiency is most common in adolescent girls who have heavy periods and poor diets?

options.A: Beriberi and Thiamine deficiency
options.B: Iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Scurvy and Vitamin C deficiency
options.D: Rickets and Vitamin D deficiency

explanation: Monthly blood loss plus meals lacking in iron easily leads to anemia. It's why adolescent girls often look pale or feel constantly tired, and why nutritional education is so crucial!

question: Which of these measurements is a standard part of checking a patient's nutrition using body measurements (anthropometry)?

options.A: Blood pressure and pulse rate
options.B: Serum electrolyte blood levels
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid pressure
options.D: Body mass index and height

explanation: Correct! Anthropometry simply means measuring the physical body—height, weight, and BMI are the most common ways we do this in the clinic.

question: Why are 4th-generation HIV tests that check for p24 antigens so helpful for early diagnosis?

options.A: They detect viral proteins before the body even finishes making antibodies.
options.B: They require no blood drawing and use only routine urine samples.
options.C: They can distinguish between HIV-1 and HIV-2 with 100% certainty instantly.
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for any follow-up confirmatory testing.

explanation: Checking for antigens lets us catch the virus early, even before antibodies show up. Brilliant concept to master!

question: Why does the color of the areola often change during pregnancy?

options.A: Poor blood circulation to the chest wall
options.B: Frequent washing with harsh soaps
options.C: Stretching of the underlying muscle tissue
options.D: Increased hormone levels stimulate pigment cells

explanation: Hormones like estrogen and progesterone stimulate melanocytes, causing the areola to darken during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h2)

question: What is the golden rule of nursing documentation when it comes to legal protection?

options.A: If it was not charted, it was not done
options.B: Only write down abnormal patient vitals
options.C: Always erase mistakes with correction fluid
options.D: Chart at the end of the week from memory

explanation: In the eyes of the law, if you didn't write it down in the chart, it never happened. Document everything you do!

question: What is the golden rule for traction weights on a patient's bed?

options.A: Allow the weights to hang freely without touching the floor
options.B: Rest the weights on the bed frame to give the patient a break
options.C: Lift the weights manually during every nursing shift change
options.D: Disconnect the weights whenever the patient wants to turn

explanation: Weights must always hang freely in the air. If they touch the bed or floor, the pulling force stops working on the bone!

question: What is point prevalence?

options.A: Tracking the death rate from a single outbreak
options.B: Predicting how long a chronic illness will last
options.C: Calculating new infections over a five-year span
options.D: Measuring disease frequency at one specific moment

explanation: Point prevalence looks at a condition at a single, exact moment in time, like a photograph. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h2)

question: How do contact tracing and patient interviews help during an outbreak?

options.A: They instantly give immunity to everyone who gets interviewed
options.B: They replace the need to run lab tests on blood samples
options.C: They stop germs from changing into stronger strains
options.D: They help track down the original source and anyone else who might be exposed

explanation: By talking to patients and tracing their steps, we can find out where they got sick and who else needs to be checked.

question: What is a very common emotional or social challenge for patients with chronic stress incontinence?

options.A: False belief that they are pregnant
options.B: Uncontrolled aggressive behavior toward caregivers
options.C: Severe memory loss and cognitive decline
options.D: Social isolation and anxiety about public leaks

explanation: The fear of leaking in public can make patients feel embarrassed, causing them to stay home and miss out on social life.

question: A community midwife discovers that local TBAs frequently perform dangerous abdominal massage on women in labor. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Ignore the practice since traditional customs cannot be changed
options.B: Engage the TBAs in training sessions to explain the risks and teach safe referral habits
options.C: Open a competing private hospital directly across the village square
options.D: Call the police to arrest every traditional birth attendant in the village immediately

explanation: Collaborative training respectful dialogue is far more effective at stopping harmful practices than outright hostility or alienation. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h7)

question: What does a significantly low glucose level in the cerebrospinal fluid usually suggest?

options.A: Recent physical exercise
options.B: A normal healthy patient
options.C: A bacterial infection
options.D: Viral meningitis illness

explanation: You got it! Bacterial germs consume glucose rapidly within the spinal fluid, making the lab numbers drop below normal.

question: A 40-year-old client with a desk job and a high body weight asks about their risk for diabetes. What is the best nursing explanation?

options.A: Physical inactivity and excess weight increase cellular resistance to insulin
options.B: High body weight prevents the kidneys from filtering normal blood sugar
options.C: Desk jobs cause the liver to stop producing necessary digestive enzymes
options.D: Sedentary habits directly destroy the beta cells inside the pancreas

explanation: Carrying extra body fat and lacking exercise make body tissues less responsive to the insulin your pancreas makes, leading to high blood sugar over time. Makes total sense when you break it down!

question: What is a key nursing responsibility regarding medication management in adult day care?

options.A: Prescribing new medications whenever a client reports mild discomfort
options.B: Manufacturing custom pharmaceutical compounds on-site for each client
options.C: Allowing clients to share their prescription drugs freely among peers
options.D: Verifying orders, administering or supervising intake, and monitoring for side effects

explanation: Nurses ensure medication safety by checking dosages, administering or supervising consumption, and watching closely for adverse reactions. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which of these is considered an environmental barrier to good communication?

options.A: Loud monitor alarms and constant hallway interruptions
options.B: A language difference between nurse and patient
options.C: A patient's severe hearing impairment or old age
options.D: Deep personal anxiety about an upcoming surgery

explanation: Yes! Noise and lack of privacy in the ward are classic environmental hurdles that make talking difficult.

question: A patient finishes metronidazole for amebic dysentery but skips the luminal agent. What is the biggest risk?

options.A: Immediate development of permanent kidney failure
options.B: Severe permanent discoloration of the skin
options.C: Total immunity to all future bacterial infections
options.D: Relapse of the infection from surviving cysts in the gut

explanation: Exactly! Leftover cysts in the gut can hatch later and bring the infection right back, even if the patient felt better temporarily.

question: Why do older adults with sensory loss often start withdrawing from social activities?

options.A: Difficulty with communication and environmental interaction creates frustration
options.B: Physical fatigue caused by overworking the remaining healthy senses
options.C: Mandatory medical quarantine protocols for sensory impairment
options.D: A sudden loss of interest in hobbies and personal relationships

explanation: Think about it: when it's exhausting just to hear what people are saying or navigate a room, socializing stops being fun and starts feeling like hard work. Patience and empathy go a long way here!

question: Which temporary side effect is very common after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis
options.B: High blood pressure requiring medication
options.C: Chills and low-grade fever
options.D: Severe permanent hair loss

explanation: You got it! Misoprostol frequently causes mild, temporary side effects like chills, nausea, or a slight fever. They pass quickly!

question: You notice a patient's family members have very different ideas about the patient's prognosis. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask the doctor to discharge the patient immediately
options.B: Ignore the disagreement since it doesn't affect physical comfort
options.C: Tell the family that only one person is correct
options.D: Assess each family member separately to understand their unique perspective

explanation: Families cope in different ways and often hold varied beliefs about an illness. Talking to them individually helps you support each person and communicate better. You are doing brilliantly!

question: Which part of the cerebellar peduncle mainly sends outgoing motor correction signals away from the cerebellum?

options.A: Posterior cerebellar peduncle
options.B: Middle cerebellar peduncle
options.C: Superior cerebellar peduncle
options.D: Inferior cerebellar peduncle

explanation: The superior peduncle acts mainly as an exit route, sending output signals from the deep cerebellar areas up to higher brain centers like the thalamus. Great job reviewing your neuro pathways!

question: Why do hospitals love using modular theatres with integrated digital control panels?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any nurses inside the room
options.B: To reduce the cost of electricity used by surgical lights
options.C: To allow patients to watch movies during local anesthesia
options.D: To streamline equipment controls and improve communication efficiency

explanation: Brilliant! Having gas outlets, lights, and communication tools in one central smart hub makes everything run much smoother during a busy case.

question: Which blood type is known as the universal red cell donor because almost anyone can safely receive it in emergencies?

options.A: Type AB positive
options.B: Type B negative
options.C: Type A positive
options.D: Type O negative

explanation: You've got this! Type O negative red cells have no main antigens, so they won't trigger an attack in most recipients.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a workplace risk assessment?

options.A: To evaluate how likely a hazard is to cause harm and determine appropriate controls
options.B: To replace all human workers with automated robotic machinery
options.C: To calculate the exact financial profit generated by each department
options.D: To find reasons to terminate employees who report minor injuries

explanation: Think of a risk assessment as looking ahead: we spot the danger, see how likely it is to hurt someone, and put rules in place to stop accidents before they happen.

question: What is the main purpose of continuous monitoring during a BCC project?

options.A: To calculate the final budget after the project ends
options.B: To replace the need for community baseline surveys
options.C: To track daily activities and correct mistakes early
options.D: To decide which nurses will be promoted next year

explanation: Monitoring happens as you go, helping you spot issues right away so you can adjust your strategy while the project is still running.

question: What is a core duty of a community health nurse during immunization outreach?

options.A: Manufacturing vaccines locally
options.B: Tracking local child growth charts
options.C: Performing major surgeries
options.D: Ordering hospital meal trays

explanation: Immunization clinics provide a great opportunity for community nurses to screen children and track their growth patterns. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h2)

question: Why are adolescents and young adults categorized as a vulnerable population regarding unintended pregnancy?

options.A: They often lack autonomy and access to correct information
options.B: They are completely banned from entering any market areas
options.C: They always reject assistance from community health workers
options.D: They possess advanced medical degrees in pharmacology

explanation: Young people frequently face barriers in accessing reproductive health services and accurate guidance due to age-related stigma. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h3)

question: A nurse wants to publish a study, but she is nervous about criticism and lacks writing experience. What is her best first step?

options.A: Pay for expensive advertising space in a national newspaper
options.B: Wait until retirement to think about sharing study findings
options.C: Collaborate with an experienced mentor for guidance and support
options.D: Hide the research data inside a private bedside locker

explanation: Exactly! Working alongside an experienced mentor helps build your confidence, polish your writing, and calm those nerves.

question: What is the main characteristic of a common vehicle outbreak?

options.A: Infection only spreads slowly from one family member to another over months
options.B: Pathogens travel exclusively through the air as dry microscopic dust
options.C: The disease can only be caught by direct physical contact in a hospital
options.D: Many people become infected simultaneously from a single contaminated source

explanation: Because a single food or water source serves many individuals, a common vehicle outbreak typically results in a sudden surge of cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h7)

question: Your patient knows how to inject their own insulin, but they need you to teach them how to calculate food portions. Which of Orem's systems is this?

options.A: Environmental control system
options.B: Supportive-educative system
options.C: Partially compensatory system
options.D: Fully compensatory system

explanation: Well done! In a supportive-educative system, the patient can do most things themselves, but they still need guidance, teaching, and support from you.

question: What is the best and most accurate lab test used to confirm chlamydia and gonorrhea infections of the cervix?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Basic metabolic serum panel
options.C: Nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)
options.D: Complete blood count with differential

explanation: NAAT is the gold-standard test because it is super sensitive at picking up bacterial DNA from a simple swab or urine sample.

question: What is the most common problem that happens with multiple pregnancies?

options.A: Macrosomia
options.B: Preterm birth
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Post-term delivery

explanation: You got it! Because the womb gets stretched out so quickly, most twins decide to arrive before hitting the full 37 weeks.

question: How often should you check vital signs during the first two hours after delivery?

options.A: Every hour
options.B: Every 4 hours
options.C: Once every shift
options.D: Every 15 minutes

explanation: Spot on! Checking vitals every fifteen minutes right after delivery helps us catch sudden bleeding or shock super early, keeping our patients safe. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: What is the main muscle cell that makes up the heart wall?

options.A: Osteocyte
options.B: Nephron
options.C: Cardiocyte
options.D: Neuron

explanation: You've got this! A cardiocyte is simply the individual muscle cell found in cardiac tissue. Nephrons are in the kidneys, neurons in the brain, and osteocytes in bones.

question: Why is a complete blood count (CBC) useful when checking a patient with an unknown fever?

options.A: It measures exact prostaglandin levels in the blood
options.B: It shows the exact brain set point
options.C: It helps tell bacterial and viral infections apart using white blood cells
options.D: It tells you which mosquito species bit the patient

explanation: You're doing great! High white blood cells usually point to bacteria, helping us choose the right care.

question: What causes the yellowish skin color seen in neonatal jaundice?

options.A: An excess of white blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: A temporary infection of the newborn's liver
options.C: Low levels of iron stored in newborn tissues
options.D: The accumulation of bilirubin in the body

explanation: Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced when red blood cells break down, and it builds up in the skin and eyes when the baby's body cannot clear it fast enough. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T017#GNS226_U3_T017_h1)

question: Which patient is the best fit for a subacute care unit?

options.A: A patient needing stable, step-down recovery after major surgery
options.B: A client needing long-term palliative care for terminal illness
options.C: An independent adult visiting a clinic for a routine checkup
options.D: A person requiring emergency trauma resuscitation in an ICU

explanation: You got it! These units are perfect for patients who are past the emergency phase but still need skilled nursing and therapy before heading home.

question: What is the main job of the fluid made by the seminal vesicles?

options.A: Storing mature sperm cells
options.B: Nourishing sperm with fructose
options.C: Lubricating the urethra
options.D: Neutralizing acidic urine

explanation: You've got this! Seminal vesicle fluid is packed with fructose, giving sperm the energy boost they need to swim toward the egg.

question: What is the normal healthy pH range for human blood?
explanation: Keep this number in your pocket—a blood pH of 7.35 to 7.45 is a vital sign range that the lungs and kidneys work hard to maintain every single day.

question: Besides giving us shape, what important minerals do our bones store for the body?

options.A: Calcium and phosphorus
options.B: Iron and magnesium
options.C: Sodium and chloride
options.D: Potassium and zinc

explanation: Think of your bones as a savings bank! They store vital minerals like calcium and phosphorus, releasing them into your bloodstream whenever your body needs a top-up.

question: Which way of moving drugs across cell membranes needs the body to spend actual energy (ATP)?

options.A: Passive diffusion
options.B: Facilitated diffusion
options.C: Simple filtration
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Just like climbing a hill requires energy, 'active' transport uses cellular energy to pump substances across membranes, often against a flow.

question: A patient starts coughing violently and turns pale while you are inserting a feeding tube. What should you do first?

options.A: Push the tube in faster to get it past the vocal cords
options.B: Give the patient a large cup of cold water to drink
options.C: Listen with your stethoscope over the left chest wall
options.D: Pull the tube back immediately because it is in the airway

explanation: Coughing and color changes indicate the tube has entered the trachea, requiring immediate withdrawal to restore breathing. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h4)

question: What important document must go with a patient when transferring her from a maternity home to a bigger hospital?

options.A: A clear and detailed referral note
options.B: A signed financial guarantee form
options.C: An inventory list of delivery room tools
options.D: A copy of the facility tax clearance certificate

explanation: Correct! The referral note tells the receiving team what has happened so far and what care she needs.

question: What is the medical term for when a patient takes many different medications at the same time?

options.A: Adverse reaction
options.B: Therapeutic synergy
options.C: Polypharmacy
options.D: Pharmacokinetics

explanation: Correct! 'Poly' means many, and 'pharmacy' means drugs. Polypharmacy simply means managing multiple medications at once.

question: A client who just got a copper IUD a month ago complains of slightly heavier periods and mild cramps. What is your best response as her nurse?

options.A: Tell her she has a dangerous infection that needs surgery
options.B: Schedule emergency surgery to close her cervix
options.C: Tell her to take it out herself at home right away
options.D: Reassure her that this is normal at first and discuss pain relief

explanation: Copper IUDs often cause heavier periods and mild cramping during the first few weeks or months. Reassure your patient—it usually settles down!

question: Why does severe pain after belly surgery put a patient at risk for lung problems like atelectasis?

options.A: Inflammation travels straight from the belly to the lungs
options.B: High blood pressure fills the lungs with fluid
options.C: Patients take shallow breaths and avoid coughing to protect their stitches
options.D: Pain meds paralyze the breathing muscles

explanation: When it hurts to move your tummy, you naturally take shallow breaths. This prevents deep breaths, causing tiny air sacs in the lungs to collapse.

question: Why must you always write down the body site (like oral or tympanic) along with the temperature number?

options.A: Different sites use completely different scales like Kelvin
options.B: Electronic health records will lock your chart without it
options.C: Hospital insurance demands the name of the device maker
options.D: Normal body temperature ranges change depending on where you measure it

explanation: Different parts of the body naturally run at slightly different baselines, so knowing the route is vital to read the results correctly.

question: A mum comes to the clinic having tummy tightening. When she walks around, the contractions stop completely and her cervix is still tightly closed. What's happening?

options.A: Rupture of membranes
options.B: Onset of the second stage
options.C: False labour contractions
options.D: Active phase true labour

explanation: These are false labour (or Braxton Hicks) contractions! True labour contractions keep getting stronger even if the mum moves around.

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do shortly after applying a warm compress?

options.A: Increase the water temperature in the basin for better effect
options.B: Leave the room to chart the entire procedure in the computer
options.C: Wrap the area tightly with waterproof adhesive tape
options.D: Check the patient's skin response within the first few minutes

explanation: Always check the skin early on to catch any redness, irritation, or signs of burning right away.

question: How should you think about a patient who comes in with general joint aches and morning stiffness?

options.A: As a routine case of temporary muscle fatigue from hard work
options.B: As a potential entry point into a complex chronic rheumatic condition
options.C: As a clear sign of an acute infectious disease requiring isolation
options.D: As someone suffering from an irreversible nutritional deficiency

explanation: Those early morning stiffness and joint aches are classic clues. They often give us our first hint that a broader inflammatory or joint issue might be developing.

question: How many main pillars make up the core safe motherhood framework?

options.A: Two
options.B: Eight
options.C: Four
options.D: Six

explanation: That's correct! The four pillars are family planning, antenatal care, safe delivery (obstetric care), and postnatal care.

question: How do we describe disease spread caused by a mosquito bite?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Direct transmission
options.C: Airborne transmission
options.D: Vehicle-borne transmission

explanation: Easy peasy! Insects like mosquitoes act as 'vectors'—little transport vehicles carrying germs from one person or animal to another.

question: A patient with a history of severe bee sting allergies is preparing for rural fieldwork in Nigeria. What essential item must you ensure they carry before they leave?

options.A: Prescribed epinephrine autoinjector
options.B: Traditional herbal mud for wound dressing
options.C: A bottle of strong perfume for protection
options.D: A pair of dark-colored gardening gloves

explanation: Excellent! Anyone with a history of severe stings must always have their epinephrine autoinjector on hand to treat accidental stings instantly.

question: What is the main job of reference apps like Zotero or Mendeley?

options.A: To write entire nursing essays and research papers
options.B: To block websites that contain plagiarized text
options.C: To store sources and automatically generate citations
options.D: To check student assignments for spelling errors only

explanation: Nice one! These tools save you stress by keeping your sources organized and generating citations for you.

question: What is the main danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their anti-seizure medication?

options.A: Provoking rebound status epilepticus
options.B: Experiencing immediate total amnesia
options.C: Developing chronic high blood pressure
options.D: Causing permanent liver failure

explanation: Abruptly stopping these meds can shock the brain chemistry and trigger severe, continuous seizures. Patient education on compliance is key!

question: According to Kübler-Ross, which stage of grief happens when a person tries to make a deal with God or fate to change what is happening?

options.A: Acceptance
options.B: Anger
options.C: Denial
options.D: Bargaining

explanation: In the bargaining stage, people try to negotiate or make promises to try and postpone or reverse an inevitable loss. You've got this!

question: What is widely known as the biggest challenge facing drug safety systems around the world?

options.A: Underreporting of adverse drug reactions
options.B: Too many digital reporting applications
options.C: Immediate withdrawal of safe medications
options.D: An excess of trained clinical investigators

explanation: Spot on! Many busy clinicians forget or fail to report side effects, meaning most mild or moderate reactions go completely undocumented.

question: How does team nursing differ from total patient care?

options.A: Total patient care involves no registered nurses at all
options.B: Total patient care is only used in surgical operating theatres
options.C: Team nursing uses a mix of different staff cadres to care for a group of patients
options.D: Team nursing requires one registered nurse to do everything alone

explanation: Well done! Total patient care means one nurse handles everything for a patient, while team nursing shares the workload among a group of mixed staff.

question: What does the 'three delays model' help nurses and midwives understand?

options.A: How long a normal labor stage is allowed to last
options.B: Why mothers experience severe delays in accessing life-saving care
options.C: When to administer routine antenatal vitamins
options.D: The exact timing of placental separation after delivery

explanation: Spot on! The three delays model looks at the barriers in seeking care, reaching a facility, and receiving treatment that contribute to maternal deaths. Every step counts!

question: What is a common result of having very restrictive abortion laws in developing countries?

options.A: Better funding and equipment for public maternity hospitals
options.B: Improved cooperation between traditional healers and doctors
options.C: The complete eradication of unintended pregnancies in society
options.D: An increase in dangerous, clandestine procedures performed by unqualified people

explanation: Correct. Making a procedure illegal doesn't stop it; it just drives desperate patients into secret, unsafe places.

question: In extended family systems, why do relatives often encourage couples to have many children?

options.A: To stop neighbors from gossiping
options.B: To reduce the cost of buying school uniforms
options.C: To qualify for free electricity vouchers
options.D: To secure lineage strength and farm labor

explanation: Correct! Historically, large families provided extra hands for farming and ensured the family name and heritage carried on.

question: What is a major economic barrier that limits a woman's healthcare autonomy?

options.A: Financial dependency on male heads of households
options.B: Too much freedom in spending personal income
options.C: An overabundance of free public health clinics
options.D: Excessive participation in local market associations

explanation: Without personal income or financial control, women often cannot afford transport fare or medical bills without male approval. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard contraindication for an intravenous pyelogram?

options.A: Severe kidney failure
options.B: Known allergy to iodine dye
options.C: Mild seasonal pollen allergy
options.D: Confirmed pregnancy

explanation: Allergies to pollen do not interfere with iodine contrast dye, whereas iodine allergies, kidney failure, and pregnancy are major contraindications. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h3)

question: A father is admitted for chronic hypertension. Why should the nurse involve his spouse and children in his discharge education?

options.A: Family members must take over the patient's job responsibilities
options.B: Hospital regulations require at least three visitors per patient
options.C: It prevents the patient from speaking to the doctor alone
options.D: The family functions as a unit, and lifestyle changes require household support

explanation: Diet and lifestyle changes are much easier to maintain when the whole family understands and participates in them. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T4#GNS112_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the typical average length of a complete ovarian cycle?

options.A: 28 days
options.B: 40 days
options.C: 14 days
options.D: 7 days

explanation: A standard text-book ovarian cycle is calculated to last about twenty-eight days, though normal variations among women are very common. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is checked as part of a psychosocial health history?

options.A: Precise surgical incision healing progress
options.B: Coping mechanisms and daily stress management
options.C: Laboratory results from routine blood tests
options.D: Blood pressure readings taken over 24 hours

explanation: Correct! A psychosocial check looks at mental wellness, stress levels, and emotional support systems.

question: How does dehydration often show up first in an older adult?

options.A: Rapid bone density increase
options.B: Excessive weight gain
options.C: High blood pressure spikes
options.D: Sudden onset of confusion

explanation: Surprise! In the elderly, dehydration doesn't just show up as dry skin—it often presents as sudden confusion or acting out of character. Always check hydration first!

question: Which measure of central tendency is appropriate for nominal data like patient blood types?

options.A: Mode
options.B: Average
options.C: Mean
options.D: Median

explanation: Blood types are categories, not numbers. Therefore, you can only count which category shows up most often—which is the mode!

question: What percentage of total hospital waste is generally made up of non-hazardous general waste?

options.A: Nearly 95 percent
options.B: About 75 to 80 percent
options.C: Exactly 50 percent
options.D: Around 10 to 15 percent

explanation: The majority of hospital waste is general refuse that poses no direct health risk and can be handled like normal household trash. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of glomeruli in the olfactory bulb?

options.A: They destroy excess odorant molecules before transduction occurs
options.B: They physically protect the brain from inhaled bacterial pathogens
options.C: They gather signals from receptors representing the same specific odor type
options.D: They pump mucus across the surface of the nasal epithelium

explanation: You got it! Glomeruli act like sorting hubs, collecting and organizing signals from thousands of similar smell receptors before passing the message along.

question: During a clinic visit, you suspect a mother cannot afford enough healthy food for her kids. What should you do?

options.A: Screen for food insecurity and connect the family with local food assistance programs
options.B: Assume the children are eating well because they do not look underweight
options.C: Prescribe expensive daily vitamin supplements without checking family resources
options.D: Advise the mother to spend less money on household electricity and clothing

explanation: Always look out for your patients' social needs! Connecting struggling families to support programs makes a real difference.

question: Why is the active management of the third stage of labor so important in nursing practice?

options.A: It speeds up the dilation of the cervix
options.B: It prevents preeclampsia from developing postpartum
options.C: It guarantees that the baby will not have jaundice
options.D: It helps prevent excessive postpartum bleeding

explanation: You nailed the final one! Using uterotonics and careful cord traction right after baby arrives is key to keeping postpartum hemorrhage at bay. Great job!

question: Which of these charting entries is poorly written?

options.A: Wound measures 3 cm by 2 cm with no foul drainage
options.B: Patient slept quietly for four hours through the night
options.C: Patient walked 20 meters in the hallway with a walker
options.D: Patient appears to be in a very bad mood today

explanation: Correct! Vague labels like 'bad mood' are judgmental. Always write down the exact behaviors you observe instead.

question: A 34-week pregnant mum comes in with painless, bright red vaginal bleeding. What condition should you suspect first?

options.A: Placenta previa
options.B: Placenta accreta
options.C: Chorioamnionitis
options.D: Placental abruption

explanation: Spot on! Classic textbook sign: painless, bright red bleeding late in pregnancy is a major red flag for placenta previa, where the placenta sits low over the cervix.

question: Why is waist circumference often a better indicator of health risks than BMI?

options.A: It changes based on leg water retention
options.B: It is impossible for athletes to get a false reading
options.C: It requires expensive laboratory machines
options.D: It specifically measures fat stored around internal abdominal organs

explanation: Waist measurements target belly fat directly, showing the hidden visceral fat around vital organs that drives heart disease risk.

question: For couples under 35 years old, how long of regular, unprotected sex without pregnancy is usually needed before diagnosing infertility?

options.A: Twelve months
options.B: Three months
options.C: Six months
options.D: Twenty-four months

explanation: You've got this! For younger couples, doctors look at a full 12 months (one year) of trying before calling it infertility. Keep going!

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?

options.A: Forgetting clinic locations
options.B: Traveling out of the country
options.C: Experiencing side effects
options.D: Changing religious beliefs

explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method.

question: What is a primary goal of performing a nursing mobility assessment?

options.A: To replace the need for physical therapy input
options.B: To determine functional capacity and plan safe care
options.C: To diagnose underlying genetic bone disorders
options.D: To measure exact daily caloric requirements

explanation: Assessing mobility shows what a patient can safely do on their own and what help they need. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h3)

question: As a nurse caring for an adolescent struggling with substance use, which of these should you NOT do?

options.A: Connecting the family with professional counseling services
options.B: Establishing a respectful therapeutic relationship
options.C: Scolding the patient publicly for poor life choices
options.D: Providing accurate and realistic health education

explanation: Well done! As nurses, we always keep our care professional and non-judgmental—never shaming or scolding our patients.

question: What is a major environmental risk factor that can push someone toward substance abuse?

options.A: Living in a house with too many windows
options.B: Having a naturally slow resting heart rate
options.C: Eating a diet low in essential vitamins
options.D: Peer pressure and easy availability of drugs

explanation: That's right! Surroundings matter a lot. Hanging out with peers who use drugs and having easy access makes it much harder to say no.

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.B: Staff, Bedside, Admission, Review
options.C: Safety, Behavior, Analysis, Response
options.D: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Action, Result

explanation: You got it! SBAR is your best friend when calling a doctor or handing over a patient. It keeps your message clear, short, and professional.

question: How do nurses use triage during a mass casualty incident?

options.A: By treating patients strictly on a first-come, first-served basis
options.B: By waiting for international doctors to arrive before touching any patient
options.C: By focusing only on patients who show no signs of physical injury
options.D: By sorting patients based on the urgency of their medical needs and survival chance

explanation: Exactly! Triage helps nurses quickly prioritize care so that the most critical patients get help first.

question: Which nail change is most commonly linked to long-term low blood oxygen levels?

options.A: Koilonychia
options.B: Yellowing
options.C: Clubbing
options.D: Paronychia

explanation: You got it! Finger clubbing—where the fingertips broaden and the nail bed softens—happens when the body has dealt with low oxygen for a long time.

question: Which of these is a major reason for internal displacement, especially in Northern Nigeria?

options.A: Strict government urban zoning laws
options.B: Voluntary migration for university education
options.C: Widespread industrial factory closures
options.D: Armed insurgency and violence

explanation: Sadly, armed conflict and insecurity force many families to flee their homes and seek safety elsewhere within the country.

question: What is the bioavailability of a medication given directly through an intravenous (IV) line?

options.A: 10 percent
options.B: 100 percent
options.C: 50 percent
options.D: 0 percent

explanation: Because IV meds go straight into your veins, they bypass the gut and liver completely. That means 100% of the dose reaches your bloodstream instantly!

question: A patient with advanced cancer starts strong opioid pain medication. What preventive care must you include?

options.A: Restricting fluid intake to prevent fluid overload from the oral medications
options.B: Encouraging a low-fiber diet to reduce gastrointestinal activity during treatment
options.C: Checking blood pressure every fifteen minutes to monitor for sudden hypertension
options.D: Administering prescribed stool softeners and laxatives to prevent opioid-induced constipation

explanation: Spot on! Opioids slow down the bowels significantly. Always team them up with a laxative to keep the patient comfortable and safe from constipation.

question: How does diluting a medication help when giving tiny doses to an infant?

options.A: It completely eliminates all potential drug side effects
options.B: It makes measuring a larger volume more accurate
options.C: It prevents the infant from developing a drug allergy
options.D: It shortens the half-life of the drug in the body

explanation: Measuring tiny drops like 0.2 mL can be nerve-wracking. Diluting lets you draw up a slightly bigger, much safer-to-measure amount!

question: What is a main goal of visiting a mother at home during the postnatal period?

options.A: To evaluate the household income level and financial status
options.B: To perform minor surgical operations on the mother
options.C: To monitor uterine involution and check maternal vital signs
options.D: To administer routine adult vaccinations to the father

explanation: Postnatal visits let you make sure the womb is shrinking back down nicely (involution) and that the mother's blood pressure and temperature are safe.

question: What is the main goal of Emergency Obstetric Care (EmOC)?

options.A: Treating sudden life-threatening pregnancy complications
options.B: Monitoring normal fetal growth during the third trimester
options.C: Providing routine antenatal counseling and vitamins
options.D: Assessing nutritional status prior to conception

explanation: You've got this! EmOC is all about handling sudden, dangerous emergencies during labor, delivery, and after birth to save both mother and baby. Great job!

question: How does the placenta give a newborn temporary protection against common infections?

options.A: By actively transferring maternal IgG antibodies across the placental membrane
options.B: By producing white blood cells that migrate into the fetal bloodstream
options.C: By filtering out all bacteria and viruses from maternal blood
options.D: By stimulating the fetal bone marrow to produce immunoglobulins

explanation: Nature's gift! The placenta lets the mother's protective IgG antibodies pass through to the baby, giving them a helpful head start against infections after birth.

question: When is a closed-ended question most helpful during an assessment?

options.A: When starting the orientation phase of an admission
options.B: When you need a quick, specific fact like a drug allergy
options.C: When you want the patient to describe their life story
options.D: When the patient is feeling anxious and needs to vent

explanation: Correct! Closed questions are great when you just need quick, straight-to-the-point facts like dates, numbers, or allergies.

question: Where is the safest place to give a vitamin K injection to a full-term newborn?

options.A: Ventral gluteal muscle
options.B: Vastus lateralis muscle
options.C: Deltoid muscle of the arm
options.D: Dorsogluteal muscle

explanation: The vastus lateralis in the outer thigh is the go-to spot! It's well-developed in newborns and keeps them safe from major nerves and blood vessels.

question: During a routine check, what does a pale, dusky, or blue-purple stoma tell you?

options.A: Inadequate blood supply to the stoma tissue
options.B: Normal healing after belly surgery
options.C: Too much fluid intake by the patient
options.D: A properly sealed ostomy appliance

explanation: Spot on. Color changes like blue, purple, or paleness mean blood flow is blocked or low—this is a true surgical emergency!

question: Why is eye care so important for a patient with Bell's palsy affecting Cranial Nerve VII?

options.A: The patient experiences excessive tearing that can blur vision permanently.
options.B: Infection in the inner ear spreads directly to the eyeball.
options.C: Increased pressure behind the eye causes the pupil to dilate permanently.
options.D: The inability to close the eyelid fully puts the cornea at risk of drying and ulceration.

explanation: Exactly right! Because Bell's palsy can stop the eye from closing all the way, we must protect the cornea from drying out.

question: A patient has fluid building up around their lungs in the pleural cavity. What main problem will this cause?

options.A: Interruption of normal brain activity
options.B: Blockage of food in the esophagus
options.C: Complete failure of the urinary bladder
options.D: Difficulty with normal lung expansion

explanation: Extra fluid takes up space, squeezing the lungs and making it hard for them to puff out fully when breathing in.

question: Where did traditional verbal handovers usually take place?

options.A: Inside the hospital pharmacy during medication restocking
options.B: In a conference room or nursing station away from the patient
options.C: Directly inside the patient's bathroom while they shower
options.D: At the hospital gates as staff members arrive for work

explanation: Traditionally, reports were given away from the clinical area, though nowadays we love doing them right at the bedside!

question: Why do nurses use standard scoring tools instead of just guessing a patient's risk level?

options.A: To ensure doctors do not have to write care plans
options.B: To obtain an objective score that guides consistent care planning
options.C: To replace the need for physical assessments on the ward
options.D: To speed up the patient discharge paperwork process

explanation: Standard tools take away personal guesswork and give the whole nursing team a clear, reliable picture of what care the patient needs.

question: During which stage of labor is the placenta delivered?

options.A: first stage
options.B: fourth stage
options.C: second stage
options.D: third stage

explanation: Spot on! The third stage is all about delivering the placenta safely after the baby is born.

question: What is the primary energy substrate used by the fetus, supplied constantly across the placenta?

options.A: Lactic acid
options.B: Glucose
options.C: Triglycerides
options.D: Amino acids

explanation: Glucose crosses the placenta easily and serves as the main fuel source for fetal metabolism and overall growth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h5)

question: What document clearly lists who is responsible for specific tasks and when they are due after a meeting?

options.A: A patient care plan
options.B: A hospital discharge summary
options.C: An annual financial budget
options.D: An action log

explanation: An action log tracks follow-up tasks with clear owners and deadlines so decisions actually get done.

question: What should you check first if the oxygen level inside the tent suddenly goes down?

options.A: The hospital's central pharmacy inventory
options.B: The expiration date of the plastic canopy
options.C: Tubing connections and canopy edge seals
options.D: The patient's blood pressure and heart rate

explanation: Always check your basics first! Loose tubing or edges that popped out from under the mattress are usually why oxygen is leaking out.

question: Why do many advanced cancer patients experience severe weight loss and muscle wasting?

options.A: Permanent blockage of the large intestine only
options.B: A total loss of the brain's thirst center
options.C: Being forced to do too much heavy exercise
options.D: Metabolic changes caused by the tumor and treatments

explanation: Cancer changes how the body uses energy, leading to a condition called cachexia where muscle and fat break down fast. Nutritional support is so vital here.

question: Why must you be extra careful when trying to use the basilic vein for venepuncture?

options.A: It lies close to the brachial artery and median nerve
options.B: It carries oxygenated blood directly from the lungs
options.C: It is too small to yield an adequate blood sample
options.D: It has thick muscular walls that resist needle entry

explanation: Be cautious with the basilic vein—major nerves and the brachial artery run right beside it, so care is needed to avoid accidental injury.

question: Why does a hurt or infected part of the body become warm and swollen?

options.A: Destruction of local nerve endings by invading bacteria
options.B: Decreased cellular activity slowing down the local metabolism
options.C: Rapid clotting of blood inside the deep muscle layers
options.D: Increased blood flow and fluid movement into the tissue

explanation: Correct! When your body sends extra blood and fluid to fight a germ at an injury site, it naturally causes warmth, redness, and swelling.

question: Why do doctors and nurses usually put a patient on a fluid diet?

options.A: To give the gastrointestinal tract a rest while providing hydration
options.B: To permanently replace normal chewing and digestive functions
options.C: To supply high levels of dietary fiber for bowel regularity
options.D: To rapidly increase body weight in malnourished individuals

explanation: When the tummy needs a break after illness or surgery, fluid diets provide easy hydration without overworking the gut. You've got this!

question: How does a nurse act as an effective patient advocate regarding diagnostic imaging?

options.A: By insisting that every patient with joint pain gets a daily CT scan.
options.B: By deciding which diagnostic test a patient needs without consulting a doctor.
options.C: By telling patients that CT scans carry zero health risks of any kind.
options.D: By questioning unneeded scans and confirming that radiation safety steps are followed.

explanation: Nurses advocate for patients by verifying clinical justification, preventing unnecessary radiation exposure, and supporting safe imaging practices. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is it important to teach patients to finish all prescribed drops even if they feel better?

options.A: Stopping early can allow the infection to return stronger
options.B: Unused drops will expire quickly on the bathroom shelf
options.C: Leftover drops can cause severe poisoning if saved
options.D: Doctors require empty bottles brought back to the clinic

explanation: Stopping medication early before all bacteria or inflammation is cleared often causes the condition to flare up again. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h9)

question: Why is patient teaching so important when managing chronic open-angle glaucoma?

options.A: Patients have to perform mini-surgeries at home
options.B: Eye drops must be mixed with clean water before every use
options.C: The disease is usually painless, so patients might skip lifelong treatment
options.D: The medications cure the underlying nerve damage quickly

explanation: Because chronic glaucoma doesn't hurt, patients often feel totally fine and forget to take their daily drops. Good teaching helps them see why consistency is life-saving for their vision.

question: How does poor nutrition in a pregnant mother directly affect her unborn baby?

options.A: It prevents the development of neonatal jaundice entirely
options.B: It causes the baby to be born with complete immunity to infections
options.C: It accelerates the closure of the infant's fontanelles
options.D: It increases the risk of low birth weight and developmental stunting

explanation: A baby's growth depends totally on what the mother eats. Poor maternal nutrition often leads to low birth weight babies who have a harder time fighting off sickness.

question: What is the most serious and permanent complication of untreated onchocerciasis?

options.A: Blindness
options.B: Paraplegia
options.C: Deafness
options.D: Kidney failure

explanation: Long-term eye inflammation from dying microfilariae eventually scars the eye tissue, leading to irreversible river blindness if left untreated.

question: What is the main reason a patient's serum bilirubin level shoots up?

options.A: Low dietary intake of essential amino acids
options.B: Excessive production of red blood cells in the kidneys
options.C: Impaired liver processing or bile duct blockage
options.D: Dehydration from severe vomiting and diarrhea

explanation: Exactly! Bilirubin builds up in the blood when the liver is struggling to process it or when something is blocking the bile passages.

question: What is behaviorism primarily focused on?

options.A: Observable and measurable external actions
options.B: Hidden emotional feelings and inner peace
options.C: Unconscious thoughts from childhood memories
options.D: Spiritual growth and personal reflection

explanation: Behaviorism keeps things simple: it looks only at what you can actually see and measure on the outside, rather than trying to guess inner thoughts.

question: What is the main goal of public health policies in government?

options.A: To stop foreign doctors from visiting
options.B: To close down all primary healthcare centers
options.C: To guide resource distribution and structure healthcare delivery
options.D: To make huge profits for drug manufacturing companies

explanation: Correct! Policies act like a roadmap. They give government agencies the rules and structure they need to organize, fund, and deliver healthcare properly.

question: Which board must review and approve any research involving human participants before data collection starts?

options.A: Institutional Review Board
options.B: Hospital Maintenance Committee
options.C: Financial Audit Committee
options.D: Nursing Licensing Board

explanation: The IRB acts as a safety shield, checking research plans to protect human participants from harm.

question: Why do functional ovarian cysts usually form during the reproductive years?

options.A: Because the uterus stops producing enough estrogen during pregnancy
options.B: Because of normal monthly hormonal changes and ovulation cycles
options.C: Due to bacterial infections traveling up from the vagina
options.D: As a direct result of eating high-fat foods and lack of exercise

explanation: You've got this! Functional cysts are simply tied to your normal monthly cycle and the hormones that control ovulation. Nothing to stress about!

question: In pharmacology, what do we mean by drug 'efficacy'?

options.A: The amount of medicine needed for pain relief
options.B: The time it takes for a drug to start working
options.C: The percentage of drug bound to plasma proteins
options.D: The maximum response a drug can produce

explanation: Efficacy is the drug's ultimate superpower—it measures how well the medication actually gets the healing job done at its best.

question: What happens as a normal body reflex when a patient is given a direct-acting vasodilator?

options.A: Profound bradycardia
options.B: Severe bronchial spasm
options.C: Reflex tachycardia
options.D: Significant hypokalemia

explanation: Spot on! When blood pressure drops suddenly from a vasodilator, your nervous system panics a bit and speeds up the heart to compensate.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced by community health nurses?

options.A: Poor road infrastructure and difficult geographical terrain
options.B: Inadequate medical supplies at primary healthcare centers
options.C: Unlimited availability of advanced surgical equipment in every village
options.D: Resistance from traditional or cultural belief systems

explanation: Community clinics rarely have unlimited advanced surgical equipment; resource scarcity is actually a major challenge in community practice. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h8)

question: What is the surest way to confirm a diagnosis of vulval cancer?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Urinalysis and culture
options.D: Tissue biopsy

explanation: Correct! Taking a small tissue sample (biopsy) is the only definitive way to confirm if a growth is truly cancerous.

question: What is the normal job of tumor suppressor genes in our bodies?

options.A: To stimulate rapid cell growth during injury
options.B: To supply blood vessels directly to growing tissues
options.C: To carry oxygen to rapidly dividing cancer cells
options.D: To slow down cell division and repair damaged DNA

explanation: Exactly! Think of tumor suppressor genes as the body's molecular brakes. They pause cell growth to fix DNA mistakes or clear out damaged cells.

question: When taking a family health history, which relatives matter most to ask about?
